sources.label: SPHMC Lemma4.6 actual numerical phase
sources.scope: This is the actual deterministic numerical kernel/first-order difference interface in Lemma4.6, conditional on the explicitly exposed normalized C2 curvature producer. The identity f=V_eta and source Lemma4.1 smoothing/curvature production remain open. It does not prove Proposition4.7 contraction/step absorption, Lemma4.8 M_kappa increment, logarithmic Lambda/B2, Khat/Kbar accuracy, invariance, repeated-history/cost, PBPS, either complete main theorem or their actual-input expected-cost composition. Khat and Kbar cannot be replaced by this K; TV closeness cannot transfer unbounded cost.

assumptions: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero, with its Borel measurable space. f:E->R is globally C2. kappa>=1 and every genuine nested second derivative satisfies (2kappa)^-1||v||^2 <= D2f(z)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every z,v. These are the normalized smoothed-potential curvature interface; f=V_eta and Lemma4.1 are independent prerequisites.

J>=2,h>0. The nodes are t_j=h/2(1-cos(j*pi/(J-1))), ell_j their actual Lagrange cardinal polynomials, Lambda=sup_{s in[0,h]} sum_j|ell_j(s)|, omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s)ds, b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds and c_j=integral_0^h(h-s)ell_j(s)ds. Assume only h^2 Lambda<=1. In particular h<=1 is derived, never added as a premise.

a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),Gamma=stdGaussian(E) product stdGaussian(E). Both Gaussian vectors are independent under Gamma and shared synchronously between compared inputs. P0=a p+sigma zeta0; Y0_j=x+t_j P0; Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij gradient f(Y0_j); Phi=(x+hP0-sum_j c_j gradient f(Y1_j),a(P0-sum_j b_j gradient f(Y1_j))+sigma zeta1). No stochastic gradient/proximal array appears.

For every pair z,zprime and every Gaussian vector zeta (not just almost surely), H_j is the ordinary Bochner integral of the Riesz-represented genuine D2f along the Y1prime_j-to-Y1_j segment; H=h^-1 sum_j b_j H_j. The source phase norm is the Euclidean L2 product WithLp2, not the default product max norm.
units.statement: At this explicit normalized C2 curvature interface, the actual exact-gradient two-Picard map Phi is measurable and defines a Markov kernel K(z)=Gamma.map(Phi_z). For every synchronously coupled input pair and every two-vector noise value, the actual integral average H is symmetric, (2kappa)^-1 I<=H<=I and ||H||op<=1. There exists a genuine continuous real linear R on the L2 phase space such that Delta1=Delta0+h*(Delta p,-H Delta x-Delta p)+R Delta0 and ||R||op<=8 Lambda h^2. R may depend on z,zprime,zeta; no measurable choice or global derivative of Phi is asserted. H, Phi, K and the remainder are constructed, not supplied as conclusion certificates.
units.formula: \Delta_1=\Delta_0+h(\Delta p,-H\Delta x-\Delta p)+\mathcal R_h\Delta_0,\quad\|\mathcal R_h\|_{\rm op}\le8\Lambda_Jh^2,\quad\frac1{2\kappa}I\preceq H\preceq I.

steps.title: Use the genuine cardinal-integral parents
steps.text: The compiled coefficient constructor supplies t_j in[0,h], the endpoint t_last=h, Lambda>=1, row absolute-integral bounds and sum b_j=h. The independent positive-weight theorem gives every b_j>=0. The endpoint c_j is exactly the last omega row. From h^2 Lambda<=1 and Lambda>=1 derive h<=1. No convenient coefficient or regularity certificates are assumed.

steps.title: Construct the real numerical phase and Gaussian kernel
steps.text: Continuity of the genuine gradient follows from C2 and the continuous Riesz identification. Finite actual Picard sums and both OU half-refreshes therefore make Phi jointly measurable. Push forward Kernel.id product Kernel.const Gamma; the two independent Gaussian coordinates are actual inputs of this same map. The law is exactly Gamma.map Phi_z. This is K with deterministic gradient f, not stochastic Khat or the conditional-mean Kbar.

steps.title: Bound the actual first Picard error
steps.text: Use the canonical Hessian-secant constructor at each Y0 pair, deriving the global gradient Lipschitz bound. Common Gaussian noise cancels, giving DeltaY0_j=Delta x+a t_j Delta p. Writing D=||Delta x||+||Delta p||, the actual E_i=-sum omega_ij Delta gradient_j has norm<=h^2 Lambda D/2. Since h^2 Lambda<=1, the loose bound ||DeltaY1_i||<=2D holds. All helpers are private algebra of this same source algorithm, with no separate proof credit.

steps.title: Produce the source integral average H
steps.text: At each actual Y1 pair call the compiled genuine Hessian-secant theorem. It produces symmetry, all-vector inherited curvature and norm<=1. Form H=h^-1 sum b_j H_j using the real ordinary-cardinal integrals. Positive b_j and sum b_j=h preserve both diagonal bounds and symmetry; the operator triangle bound gives norm<=1. The source H is this exact integral average, not an arbitrary matrix satisfying the desired result.

steps.title: Expand both real endpoint residuals with explicit constants
steps.text: The exact endpoint differences are Delta x+ah Delta p-sum c_j H_j DeltaY1_j and a^2 Delta p-a sum b_j H_j DeltaY1_j. The scalar exponential inequalities give |1-a|<=h/2 and |a^2-1+h|<=h^2. Let e=h^2 Lambda/2. The position residual has norm<=h^2||Delta p||/2+h^2 Lambda D. The momentum residual has norm<=h^2||Delta p||+h^2||Delta x||/2+h(h||Delta p||+eD). With h<=1 and Lambda>=1 their sum is <=4h^2 Lambda D (in particular bounds 3/2 and 5/2 times h^2 Lambda D). These are actual residuals, not hypotheses.

steps.title: Use the source Euclidean phase norm
steps.text: The L2 product norm satisfies ||(rx,rp)||2<=||rx||+||rp|| and each coordinate norm is <=||(Delta x,Delta p)||2. Hence D<=2||Delta0||2, giving actual residual norm<=8 Lambda h^2||Delta0||2. This avoids using the default max norm as if it were the Euclidean norm.

steps.title: Construct the pointwise linear remainder
steps.text: If Delta0=0, the derived residual bound forces r=0 and R=0 works. Otherwise define Rw=inner(Delta0,w) r/||Delta0||^2 using Mathlib rankOne. It satisfies R Delta0=r; its operator norm is <=||r||/||Delta0||<=8 Lambda h^2. This explicitly elaborates the source existential remainder and omitted universal constant. It is not a differentiability/Jacobian claim or a measurable operator-choice claim.
